pk.context: 5 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: Acts on both free and clot-bound factor Xa without needing antithrombin III; only about 27% of clearance is renal.

clues.text: Bioavailability is about 50% at doses up to 10 mg, and food does not affect it. About 87% is bound to plasma protein; CYP3A4 metabolism is the main route, with renal excretion about 27% of clearance.
The drug substance is a white to pale-yellow powder with a molecular weight of 459.5.
Approved under an NDA as 2.5 mg and 5 mg tablets, plus a 0.5 mg tablet for oral suspension.

Boxed for thrombotic events after premature discontinuation and for spinal/epidural hematoma. Contraindicated in active pathological bleeding and severe hypersensitivity; bleeding is the main adverse reaction.
Reducing stroke and systemic embolism in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation; preventing deep vein thrombosis after hip or knee replacement; treating deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
A selective inhibitor of factor Xa that acts on both free and clot-bound enzyme, reducing thrombin generation. It needs no antithrombin III for its antithrombotic effect.
The generic name begins with A and has eight letters.
